description:
README Status paragraph (numbers, wf6/structs contribution only, to be re-counted after the round merges): 13,338 lines of hand-written Lean across 30 files (plus 421 generated lines in eight Gen/ files), 731 theorems, zero sorry and zero axiom. Eight worked examples (bank, lock, supervisor, task, watchdog, ttl, registry, ringlog). The translator suite is 42 regression fixtures (32 ok, 10 error).

README table row to add: | Ringlog | count equals the queue length and never exceeds max_entries | 9,348 |

README Layout rows to add:
| Leanactors/Gen/Ringlog.lean | Generated from elixir/src/ringlog.ex: the Entry structure with defaults, the Level enum, and the store's state flattened into .ringlog (entries : List Entry) (count : Nat) (max_entries : Nat) |
| Leanactors/Examples/Ringlog.lean | Ring buffer of log entries: hand model, beh_eq_gen, the bounded check of count = entries.length and count <= max_entries (9,348 configurations, two mutants caught in 7), and the proof -- ok_step for one behaviour step, beh_no_spawn, count_invariant for every reachable configuration |
| elixir/src/ringlog.ex | A GenServer whose state is its own struct: a queue of %Entry{} with a count and a cap; casts push and drop the oldest when full, calls return every entry or only those of one level |
| elixir/ringlog.exs | The BEAM twin of Examples/Ringlog.lean |
| elixir/test/fixtures/structs.ex, enum_list.ex, queue.ex | Fixtures for the three new translator features (each also compiled by lake env lean) |

README, a new paragraph after the Maps paragraph:

Structs. `defstruct f: d, ..` with `@type t :: %__MODULE__{f: T, ..}` becomes a Lean `structure` whose fields carry the defstruct defaults, so `%Mod{f: e}` is `({ f := e } : Mod)`, `x.f` is the projection and `%Mod{f: p}` a pattern on the anonymous constructor. When a GenServer's `@type state` is its own struct -- the shape of a real Phoenix `LogStore` -- the struct is flattened into that module's state constructor, one Lean field per defstruct field: `state.f` is the part the clause's pattern bound to f and `%{state | f: e}` rebuilds the constructor with the named parts replaced. Nothing else in the translator changes, which is the point of the flattening: field coverage, crash clauses, the whole-state alias and the hidden `gen` field of a receive loop all keep working. Enum over lists is the List API (filter/map/reject/count/any?/all?/member?/reverse/take/drop/at/empty?, `length`, `hd`/`tl`, `++` and the comprehension `for x <- l, c, do: e`), with `fn x -> e end` and the capture `&(&1.f == v)` as Lean lambdas; `hd` is `List.headD` at the element type's default, because it raises on the BEAM and an expression in the model cannot. An Erlang queue is the list, oldest first: `:queue.in` appends, `{_, q} = :queue.out(q0)` is `let q := List.tail q0`, `:queue.to_list` is the identity and `case :queue.out(q)` matches head and rest at once.

NOTES round-6 bullet for this piece:

structs, Enum and :queue (node 561). The target was `Ensemble.LogStore`, a ring buffer whose state is its own struct. Two shapes were on the table (567, 569): keep the state as one Lean field of a `structure`, or flatten the struct into the state constructor. Flattening won (570) because everything the translator already does to a multi-field state -- coverage of the fields, the crash clauses, the whole-state alias a fallthrough needs, the hidden generation field of a receive loop -- keeps working unchanged, and the Gen files stay in the shape the proofs read. The cost is that a value of the state's struct type never exists in the model, so binding one is a translator error with a message saying to return the state or bind its fields. Three things surprised (610): Lean has no forward references, so declarations had to be emitted in dependency order once a struct could appear inside a tagged union; a whole-state part the body never mentions trips the unused-variable linter, so it is renamed `_part`; and an .exs driver cannot write `%Entry{}` at all, because a script is expanded before its `Code.require_file` has run. The ringlog invariant (count is the queue's length, and at most the cap) is proved the cheap way: `ok_step` says one behaviour step preserves it, `beh_no_spawn` says the behaviour emits no spawning effect, and `SysStep.stateOf_spawn_cases` from SysProps turns those two into `count_invariant` over every configuration reachable under unbounded scheduling. No generic lemma was added to SysProps, Fair or AssocList (609).
